first.rationale:
The loudest signal is competitive price pressure, which points at promotional_pricing via memory_73. That is exactly why memory_73 is the first thing I want verified rather than the first thing I act on. Its consolidated summary is unusually broad for a single record (acquisition lift, revenue lift, faster time-to-first-value, holds across both billing plans), which is the shape a claim takes after it has been compressed and re-summarized across sessions. Discount-led acquisition is also the direction with the worst failure mode against the stated objective: it can post strong short-run acquisition and revenue while importing price-sensitive, churn-prone accounts, so the 'revenue lift' is only qualified revenue if the archived record actually measured retention and margin, not just bookings. Matching a competitor's entry price also risks resetting our own price anchor, which is hard to undo. I will not commit to it on a summary alone.

Second verification goes to memory_86 because it is the memory I actually intend to act on. Two of the three symptoms are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), which are internal funnel problems rather than pricing problems, and they are the ones most plausibly within reach in one week. memory_86 and memory_31 point the same way from different angles (shortening onboarding, cutting signup fields), and memory_91 says activation messaging also moved week-one engagement. I want the memory_86 source record to tell me whether the completion lift actually carried through to downstream qualified revenue or only to a completion-rate metric, since 'completion went up' is easy to achieve by removing steps and can be self-defeating if those steps were doing qualification work.

That is the residual risk on my own pick: memory_31's field-cutting and memory_86's step-cutting both make it cheaper to enter the funnel, which can raise activation counts while diluting lead quality. Under a sustainable-qualified-revenue objective I will instrument this on downstream qualified conversion, not just completion and week-one activation. Standard experiment scale, not broad rollout, because the two supporting memories are consolidated summaries whose downstream revenue linkage is still unconfirmed. If memory_86 verifies weakly or turns out to be completion-only, activation_messaging (memory_91) is my fallback for the slot; if memory_73 verifies strongly with retention data intact, promotional_pricing becomes viable next cycle but as a small guarded test on a bounded SMB segment, not a broad price move.
